83-type signature corresponding to InsDel9 (C_ID9)

Note

We believe that the signature C_ID9 that we extracted corresponds to COSMIC signature ID9, even though C_ID9 has a large proportion of deletions of single thymines in long poly-T contexts, which ID9 completely lacks. We believe this is an instance of “over splitting” due to all such deletions being allocated to a single mutation type in the 83-type indel classification.

Furthermore, Koh, Nanda, et al.’s extraction of a similar signature from 89-type spectra and our extraction from type-476 spectra that collapse to a similar 89-type signature indicate noticeable proportions of insertions of single Ts in long poly-T contexts.

ID9 also lacks insertions and deletions of sequences longer than 1 base, but these insertions and deletions are present in C_ID9 and in extractions from 89-type and 476-type spectra, which would seem to support C_ID9 versus ID9.

83-type signature converted from signature discovered in the 476-type spectra (using bipartite matching optimization) | cosine similarity to C_ID9: 0.9983

Click to see flow diagrams: 476-type to 83-type collapse

These Sankey diagrams show how the 476-type mutation categories are redistributed to 83-type categories using bipartite matching. We only show the diagrams for insertions or deletions of > 1 base because it is for these indels that 476-type categories map to > 1 83-type category.
